records.Japanese:
これで全ての『覇者の証』が
そろったわけね…
records.speaker: Maria Li
records.source_meaning: Maria observes that they now have all the Proofs of Conquest.
records.context: All Proofs gathered;the crew expects a marvel,then Maria explains collective belief and the Imperial Seal analogy. Hope for peace yields to responsibility and affectionate retirement/work banter before returning to Hangzhou. Conditional companion alternatives remain distinct.
records.localization_note: Maria counts the completed set aloud. The tentative pause leaves room for Xien to observe that nothing happens.

records.Japanese:
『覇者の証』は、その地方で
信奉されていた神や英雄、伝説に
まつわる遺物だった。もちろん
本物かどうかも怪しいものよ
records.current_English:
The Proofs were relics tied to     
 gods, heroes, and legends
 revered in each region. Who knows
 if they're even genuine?
records.speaker: Maria Li
records.previous_English: The Proofs were relics tied to gods, heroes, and legends revered in each region. Who knows if they're even genuine?
records.english: The Proofs were relics tied to gods, heroes, and legends revered in each region. Who knows if they're even genuine?

records.source_meaning: The Proofs were relics connected to gods,heroes or legends revered in each region;even their authenticity is questionable,not categorically disproven.
records.context: All Proofs gathered;the crew expects a marvel,then Maria explains collective belief and the Imperial Seal analogy. Hope for peace yields to responsibility and affectionate retirement/work banter before returning to Hangzhou. Conditional companion alternatives remain distinct.
records.localization_note: Maria questions authenticity after describing what each region revered. Keep the uncertainty on a complete line before she turns to the power of belief.

いえ、きっと提督のおっしゃるとおり
『証』を手にした我々の努力次第
ということなのでしょう
records.current_English:
No, Admiral. I'm sure you're right.
 Now that we hold the Proofs, 
 it depends on what we do with them.
records.speaker: Ian Dukov
records.previous_English: No, Admiral. I'm sure you're right. Now that we hold the Proofs, it depends on what we do with them.
records.english: No, Admiral. I'm sure you're right. Now that we hold the Proofs, it depends on what we do with them.
records.source_meaning: A companion disagrees that it sounds trite and respectfully says it must depend on the efforts of them,the new Proof holders,as she says.
records.context: All Proofs gathered;the crew expects a marvel,then Maria explains collective belief and the Imperial Seal analogy. Hope for peace yields to responsibility and affectionate retirement/work banter before returning to Hangzhou. Conditional companion alternatives remain distinct.
records.localization_note: Ian respectfully agrees while putting responsibility on what they do as holders of the Proofs. His words lead directly into Xien's joke about postponing retirement.

records.Japanese:
ああ！　いよいよ大勢の面前に出るの
ですね！　わ、私はモーレツに
キンチョーしてきましたです！
records.current_English:
Oh! It's time to go out
 in front of all those people!
 I-I'm getting awfully nervous!
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.previous_English: Oh! It's time to go out in front of all those people! I-I'm getting awfully nervous!
records.english: Oh! We're finally going out there in front of all those people! I-I'm getting awfully nervous!
records.source_meaning: A nervous companion realizes they are finally about to appear before a great crowd and becomes intensely nervous,with a stammer.
records.context: Ending variant repeats the Proof discussion,then the crew jokingly practices formal military address as Maria prepares to review the Ming forces. Her command leads into the narrator's uncertain historical epilogue. Preserve sentence continuity across FE panels and the comic register corrections.
records.localization_note: Cesare realizes the wait is over and the whole group must face the crowd. Keep his alarm and nervous stammer before Maria's brisk order.

lines: Oh! We're finally going out there
in front of all those people!

records.Japanese:
（おかしいな…、船に乗ったはずじゃ…
　まあ、いいか
　こうしてビアンカもいるしな。）
records.current_English:
(That's strange... I could've sworn
 I was on a ship. Oh, well. 
 Bianca's here.)
records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.previous_English: (That's strange... I could've sworn I was on a ship. Oh, well. Bianca's here.)
records.english: (That's strange... I could've sworn I was on a ship. Oh, well. Bianca's here.)
records.source_meaning: Angelo privately thinks he had boarded a ship,but lets the discrepancy go because Bianca is here.
records.context: Angelo collapses in fever. A Bianca-labeled dream recalls flowers,their childhood promise and the search for his sister;she urges him to live with his new family. He wakes with a changed view while companions still urge the search. Preserve grief and uncertainty without explaining the dream's metaphysics or adding a diagnosis.
records.localization_note: Angelo thinks he had been aboard a ship. His quiet decision to let the inconsistency go rests on Bianca being beside him. Keep the parentheses for his private thought.

lines: I was on a ship. Oh, well.

records.Japanese:
行くなよ…
おいおい、冗談きついぜ
records.current_English:
Don't go... Come on. 
 This isn't funny.
records.speaker: Angelo Puccini
records.previous_English: Don't go... Come on. This isn't funny.
records.english: Don't go... Come on. This isn't funny.
records.source_meaning: Angelo begs her not to go and protests that this is a cruel joke.
records.context: Angelo collapses in fever. A Bianca-labeled dream recalls flowers,their childhood promise and the search for his sister;she urges him to live with his new family. He wakes with a changed view while companions still urge the search. Preserve grief and uncertainty without explaining the dream's metaphysics or adding a diagnosis.
records.localization_note: Angelo pleads with Bianca and tries to dismiss the farewell as a cruel joke. The three short beats preserve his denial before the more desperate plea.

records.Japanese:
お初にお目にかかります
私はミっヴォール！
ミヴォール・ゲンツと申します
以後お見知りおきをっ
records.current_English:
A pleasure! I'm M-Mivor! 
 Mivor Genz. At your service!
records.speaker: Mivor Genz
records.previous_English: A pleasure! I'm M-Mivor! Mivor Genz. At your service!
records.english: A pleasure! I'm M-Mivor! Mivor Genz. At your service!
records.source_meaning: He formally introduces himself,stammering Mivor/Mivoll from ミヴォール・ゲンツ;approved name spelling remains to bind rather than guess.
records.context: Cristina rejects a persistent suitor and an engagement arranged without her consent. Her actual grandfather offers travel and sword training;Maria invites both,but his fear of water and futile duel fuel the comedy. Preserve nonreciprocal affection,explicit kinship,gender obstacle and no invented wager.
records.localization_note: Mivor stumbles over his own name and overdoes the formal courtesy. His full name and enthusiastic introduction play against Cristina's lack of interest.

records.Japanese:
ああ、もう、うるさい！
早く出港しましょうよ！
こいつ、うっとうしいから！
records.current_English:
Oh, enough already!
 Can we set sail? 
 He's driving me crazy!
records.speaker: Cristina Erneco
records.previous_English: Oh, enough already! Can we set sail? He's driving me crazy!
records.english: Oh, will you pipe down? Let's set sail already. He's driving me crazy!
records.source_meaning: Cristina snaps that he is loud andannoying andurges the group to set sail soon to get away from him.
records.context: Cristina returns briefly to her hometown London and encounters her unwanted suitor Mivor. She rejects marriage again. A drowning boy panics and pulls her under;Mivor overcomes his established fear of water to rescue them. Cristina initially doubts him,then the mother confirms his courage. Her awkward thanks reignites his exuberant courtship despite her protest;Maria privately finds them well matched. Keep Cristina independent,Mivor comically effusive and the rescue frightening. The boy and rescuers are not siblings. The FE boy voices are explicitly labeled unseen speech,not narrator oractor254. The comparison signs express fear versus Cristina.
records.localization_note: Cristina snaps at the noisy Mivor, then urges the group to leave before he can keep at it. The change makes both addressees clear.

records.Japanese:
はい。機械が好きなので
船の扱いや修理なんかが得意です
records.current_English:
Yes. I like machinery. 
 I'm good with ships, 
 and I can fix them, too.
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.previous_English: Yes. I like machinery. I'm good with ships, and I can fix them, too.
records.english: Yes. I like machinery. I'm good at handling ships. I can fix them, too.
records.source_meaning: Janus likes machinery andis good at handling ships andmaking repairs.
records.context: Janus approaches Maria for work andproposes a1000-gold condition. Richard objects to his apparent impudence. The payment branch waits one day andreveals he repaired a ship andpaid his debts,testing whether Maria has the stature of an admiral he can trust with his life. He offers the ship andmisunderstands her request for his own name. The alternative refusal branch says she lacks that much money andhe will try elsewhere. The FE instruction explains retrieving/renaming the ship. Do not combine alternatives into one earned outcome.
records.localization_note: Janus answers Maria's general question with his interest in machinery and both specific skills he brings. He can handle ships and make repairs.

records.Japanese:
誰に向かって口をきいているのか
分かっておるのか！
records.current_English: Do you know who you're talking to?!
records.speaker: Richard Townsend
records.previous_English: Do you know who you're talking to?!
records.english: Do you know who you're talking to?!
records.source_meaning: Richard demands whether Janus realizes whom he is addressing. Preserve his presumptuous indignation without inventing a formal court rank.
records.context: Janus approaches Maria for work andproposes a1000-gold condition. Richard objects to his apparent impudence. The payment branch waits one day andreveals he repaired a ship andpaid his debts,testing whether Maria has the stature of an admiral he can trust with his life. He offers the ship andmisunderstands her request for his own name. The alternative refusal branch says she lacks that much money andhe will try elsewhere. The FE instruction explains retrieving/renaming the ship. Do not combine alternatives into one earned outcome.
records.localization_note: Richard rebukes Janus for presuming on the admiral's good will. The sharp spoken question carries his indignation without assigning a new rank.

lines: Do you know who you're talking to?!

records.Japanese:
おじさん？　後にしてくださいよ
今すごく忙しいんですよ。もう少しで
僕の理論が証明できそうなところに…
records.current_English:
Oh, it's you. Can it wait? 
 I'm busy.
 I'm close to proving my theory...
records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.previous_English: Oh, it's you. Can it wait? I'm busy. I'm close to proving my theory...
records.english: Oh, it's you. I'm busy. Can we talk later? I've almost proved my theory...
records.source_meaning: Charles recognizes the older man andasks him to come later because he is extremely busy andalmost ready to prove his theory. Uncle is familiar address,not kinship.
records.context: A blast interrupts Maria andXien on reaching the far West from the East. A shipyard man complains about Charles's repeated science experiments. Maria is interested in science changing daily life;Xien infers his bomb knowledge could help gunnery. They recruit the excitable,self-important scientist after Xien praises Maria in an explicitly abridged account. Maria's polite elderly-gentleman introduction prompts Xien's comic protest. No blood relationship between Charles andthe shipyard man is established.
records.localization_note: Charles recognizes his visitor without suggesting kinship and tries to put him off. His sudden enthusiasm about being close to proof explains the hurry.

そう思うのも無理はないじゃろうて
records.current_English:
Well, I can't blame you if you 
 don't know who you're talking to.
records.speaker: Xien Yan
records.previous_English: Well, I can't blame you if you don't know who you're talking to.
records.english: Well, I can't blame you if you don't know who you're talking to.
records.source_meaning: Xien says it is understandable he thinks that if he does not know whom he is addressing.

Maria is interested in science changing daily life;Xien infers his bomb knowledge could help gunnery. No blood relationship between Charles andthe shipyard man is established.

records.Japanese:
わあ、楽しそうだなあ。私は
シャルル・ジャン・ロシュフォールです
よろしくお願いします！
records.current_English:
Oh, this sounds like fun!
 I'm Charles Jean Rochefort.
 Pleased to meet you!
records.speaker: Charles Rochefort
records.previous_English: Oh, this sounds like fun! I'm Charles Jean Rochefort. Pleased to meet you!
records.english: Oh, this sounds like fun! I'm Charles Jean Rochefort. Pleased to meet you!
records.source_meaning: Charles says this sounds fun andintroduces his full name as Charles Jean Rochefort,with a polite greeting. Final field spelling remains subject to the scoped name reconciliation.
records.context: A blast interrupts Maria andXien on reaching the far West from the East. A shipyard man complains about Charles's repeated science experiments. Maria is interested in science changing daily life;Xien infers his bomb knowledge could help gunnery. They recruit the excitable,self-important scientist after Xien praises Maria in an explicitly abridged account. Maria's polite elderly-gentleman introduction prompts Xien's comic protest. No blood relationship between Charles andthe shipyard man is established.
records.localization_note: Charles is delighted and introduces himself with his complete spoken name. This is a personal introduction following Maria's and Xien's exchange about being elderly.

records.Japanese:
ここで、船が着くたびに
こうして声を掛けていたんだ
あんたたちでちょうど１００人目だ
records.current_English:
I ask every time a ship comes in.
 You're the hundredth person
 I've asked.
records.speaker: Sailor
records.previous_English: I ask every time a ship comes in. You're the hundredth person I've asked.
records.english: I call out as each ship comes in. You're the hundredth I've asked.
records.source_meaning: He has been calling out whenever a ship arrives,andthey are the100th person/group he has approached. Preserve100 without inventing elapsed days or100 ships wrecked.
records.context: An abrasive former sailor asks whether Maria believes in miracles. In the belief branch he initially insults her,then reveals bitterness about unbelieving captains andgives her a bullet pendant because she believes. He has asked100 captains/groups andcan no longer sail for an unspecified physical reason. The FE Luck increases belong to this result. The disbelief branch has Fernando dismiss the encounter andFE Spirit increases. Preserve each branch andthe exact +1 messages;do not claim both outcomes occur together or invent the man's injury.
records.localization_note: The sailor says he has been approaching arriving sailors here to find a captain who believes in miracles. Keep the repeated effort and the exact count without inventing its duration.

lines: I call out as each ship comes in.
